next: Wednesday afternoon or evening once the showers are gone and the noon king tide has passed, sooner if a morning shower turns heavy or NWS issues a flood product for the Peninsula; a short quiet note after the Coastal Flood Warning ends Thursday afternoon
headline: The overnight burst ECMWF showed did not stay in the guidance: all models now keep the wettest 3 hours under 0.1 in, with the last showers most likely around 6 to 8:30 AM; the rating card stays at none, and the noon king tide on the Bay shore is today's main hazard.

summary.text: Shifted since yesterday afternoon: ECMWF dropped from 0.27 to 0.01 in, HRRR rose from 0.02 to 0.09 in, and the peak moved from 2–5 AM to roughly 6–8:30 AM. Consensus 0.08 in, about unchanged.
Wettest 3 hours: HRRR 0.09 (GFS copies it), NBM 0.08, RRFS 0.03, ECMWF 0.01 in. HRRR 15-minute is wettest at 0.23 in over about 6 to 8:45 AM. All far below thresholds.
Rating card consensus 0.08 in: none. A heavier post-frontal shower could pond gutters briefly. Yellow (garage) needs about 0.71 in in 3 hours or a 0.40 in hour; the strongest model hour is 0.16 in.
Scattered showers until about 9 AM, most likely around 6 to 7:30 AM; dry by late morning. Dry Thanksgiving through Saturday; NWS expects a weak system Sunday and a stronger storm early next week.
Showers fall near the 6:14 AM low (running about 4.4 ft with surge), so the channel can drain. Channel at Alameda 0.15 ft at 4 AM, far below Flood Monitoring 3.18 ft.
No need to move cars. Stay off the Bay shore, sloughs and shoreline roads around the noon king tide today (about 11 ft) and 1 PM Thursday. Use the dry days to clear drains before Sunday.

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text:
The cold front came through overnight and is dissipating as it exits east. NWS San Francisco's short-term discussion (11:10 PM Tuesday) described warning operations for the North Bay, where hourly rates of 0.25 to 0.5 in were observed, and a second round of convective showers behind the front into Wednesday morning, with flooding concerns through late morning. The newer 3:48 AM aviation discussion says the front is dissipating and the last showers are moving out, with VFR conditions and calm winds near SFO. High-resolution guidance has showers out of the area by late morning, then dry through Saturday. Radiation fog is possible tonight. NWS expects a weak system Sunday (heaviest in the North Bay and Santa Cruz Mountains, lighter elsewhere) and a stronger storm early to mid next week, similar to last week's.

The Coastal Flood Warning for the San Francisco and San Pablo Bay shorelines remains in effect until 4 PM Thursday.

sections.title: What changed and model trends
sections.text:
Since the 4:25 PM Tuesday discussion the overnight picture flipped. ECMWF, then the wettest model with 0.27 in in 3 hours around 2 to 5 AM, now has only a trace (0.01 in) ahead. HRRR, then nearly dry, now carries morning showers. The street's flood risk did not change: every model stays well under 0.25 in in 3 hours, so the rating card remains at none.

Wettest 3 hours / total, 4 AM Wednesday onward (72 hours):
• HRRR (2 AM Wed run, out to 10 PM Thu): 0.09 / 0.13 in, three showers of 0.04 in each between about 4 and 8 AM. Up from 0.02 / 0.02 in.
• HRRR 15-minute (ends 11:45 PM Thu): 0.27 in total, wettest 3 hours 0.23 in over about 6 to 8:45 AM, and its hardest hour 0.16 in around 6:30 to 7:15 AM. This series is wetter than the hourly HRRR.
• NBM: 0.08 / 0.10 in, mostly a 0.07 in hour around 6 AM.
• RRFS (4 PM Tue run, no newer run yet): 0.03 / 0.04 in, around 4 to 5 AM.
• ECMWF: 0.01 / 0.01 in. Down from 0.27 / 0.37 in.
• GFS: matches HRRR hour for hour again, no independent information.

Consensus (HRRR 0.09 × 1.25 = 0.11, RRFS 0.03, NBM 0.08): middle value 0.08 in, versus 0.07 in yesterday afternoon. I think none is right. Even the wetter HRRR 15-minute numbers with the 1.25 bias (about 0.29 in in 3 hours) stay far below Yellow at 0.71 in. The 6 AM shower has some support (HRRR and NBM both show it), so expect a brief wet spell around the morning commute rather than an isolated model artifact; NWS's point about stronger showers once the sun comes out is the main reason not to call it completely over.

sections.title: Tide and the channel
sections.text:
NOAA's Bay model (run ends 1 AM Friday) still runs about 1.2 to 1.6 ft above the predicted tides at Redwood City. The 7.1 ft high at 1:12 AM ran about 8.7 ft. The 3.2 ft low at 6:14 AM runs about 4.4 ft near 6:30 AM, and the water is only back to about 5.7 ft at 8 AM, so this morning's showers fall during the best drainage window of the day.

The 9.5 ft king tide at 11:46 AM runs about 11.1 ft at noon, after the showers end. Tonight's -1.7 ft low at 7:17 PM runs about -0.2 ft. Thursday: 7.1 ft high at 2:08 AM (about 8.7 ft) and the 9.4 ft high at 12:35 PM (about 10.9 ft near 1 PM). Friday's 9.1 ft high is at 1:28 PM.

NWS: at the San Francisco gauge, highs 2.7 ft above normal today (8.5 ft at 10:49 AM), 2.2 ft Thursday, and 2.0 ft Friday and Saturday, including up to 1.6 ft of surge, approaching the highest tide ever recorded there. These tides matter for the Bay shore, not for Athlone Terrace directly; they would only slow the channel if heavy rain coincided with them, which is not forecast.

Channel: at Alameda de las Pulgas 0.15 ft at 4 AM, up slightly from 0.12 to 0.13 ft through the night (Flood Monitoring 3.18 ft, Watch 4.6 ft, Warning 5.65 ft). Upstream of Caltrain: 0.07 ft at 5:13 PM Tuesday, still its latest report (Flood Monitoring 2.8 ft).

sections.title: Current observations
sections.text: The Caltrain rain gauge has not reported since 5:13 PM Tuesday (no rain in the 24 hours to then), so there is no local measurement of how much fell overnight. The small rise at the Alameda channel gauge, 0.12 to 0.15 ft between 3 and 4 AM, suggests only light rain so far. NWS reports the front dissipating, with VFR and calm conditions near SFO.

sections.title: Uncertainty
sections.text: Low concern for flooding. The models still disagree on amounts (ECMWF 0.01 in to HRRR 15-minute 0.23 in in 3 hours), and RRFS is 12 hours old, but no source comes within a third of the Yellow threshold. The open question is a heavier convective shower behind the front this morning; NWS flagged that risk overnight, but the most such a cell would likely do here is pond gutters and low spots briefly.

sections.title: What to do
sections.text:
• This morning: no need to move cars out of the cul-de-sac. If a heavy shower does hit, take timestamped photos of the street.
• Today and Thursday: stay away from the Bay shore, tidal sloughs and low shoreline roads around the late-morning and early-afternoon king tides; don't walk or drive through moving water.
• Thursday through Saturday: use the dry days to clear leaves from street drain grates and yard drains and secure outdoor decorations before Sunday's rain and next week's stronger storm.
• Watch for fog tonight if traveling for Thanksgiving.
